Onboarding showcase film posters (frames of the project-authored films)
========================================================================

Vendored asset:  ../src/main/res/drawable-nodpi/ — ten lossless WebP files at
                 720 x 900, totalling 369,494 bytes. Eight are final frames,
                 one per film cut; two are shared light/dark start frames.
Owner:           TaffyGo for the original compositions, copy, drawn UI, TaffyGo
                 marks and the act of selecting and encoding these frames.
Licence:         TaffyGo's original work is reserved media rather than code
                 licensed under the repository LICENSE; see TRADEMARKS.md. Space Grotesk is used under the SIL Open Font License
                 1.1. No third-party logo or product artwork appears in any of
                 the ten files recorded here; `showcase-films.txt` states the
                 same for their films and holds the rights reasoning for both
                 records.
Audio:           None. A poster is a still image and carries no part of the
                 procedural sound design embedded in the MP4s.
Upstream:        Captured from the project-authored HyperFrames browser
                 timeline described by `showcase-films.txt`, then resized and
                 encoded losslessly. They were rendered, not fetched.
Fetched:         NOT APPLICABLE.
Recorded:        2026-08-23. The bytes and their 2026-08-21 record are older
                 than this date; what changed on 2026-08-23 is which files are
                 in the directory.

Six posters left with their films
---------------------------------

The 2026-08-21 record covered sixteen posters, of which six were the light and
dark final frames of `compare`, `driving-licence` and `mail`. Those three films
composite official third-party and Government of India artwork with no recorded
permission, which is OD-094 in `docs/open-decisions.md`, and their final frames
carry the same artwork behind the closing card. Films and posters are one
rights question, so the six left with the three films rather than being kept as
stills of something that may not ship.

A poster leaves with its film and returns with it. There is no case in which
this directory holds a final frame whose MP4 is not in `res/raw`, and the
bidirectional check below is what makes that structural rather than a
convention someone remembers.

Checksums and byte counts of the shipped WebP files
---------------------------------------------------

The `sha256_` and `bytes_` facts are checked against every file in
`res/drawable-nodpi` in both directions by `tools/lib/vendored_assets.py`.
A line here with no file on disk is a finding, and so is a file with no line.

All twenty facts are the values the 2026-08-21 record carried, re-verified
against the file on disk on 2026-08-23. No poster was re-encoded.

Generation and content
----------------------

The final frames and the two shared start frames were captured from the browser
timeline as PNGs, then encoded with:

  cwebp -lossless -z 9 -resize 720 900 -metadata none \
    <snapshot.png> -o <poster.webp>

Read from the files on 2026-08-23: all ten are RIFF/WebP containers whose
`WEBP` fourcc is followed directly by a `VP8L` chunk, at 720 x 900 with an
alpha channel. A file in that simple lossless form carries no `VP8X` chunk and
therefore no EXIF, XMP or ICC block, which is the same claim the earlier record
made and the reason `-metadata none` is in the command above.

The two shared start posters are plain theme surfaces: 462 and 498 bytes of
flat colour, one per theme, shown by every prefetched page before its decoder
exists. They contain no mark of any kind.

The eight final posters contain no third-party logo or product image. All of
them use Space Grotesk; page-tools also contains the repository-owned synthetic
diagram fixture. Exact frozen visual source hashes, ownership boundaries and
licence status are in `showcase-films.txt` and apply unchanged here.

Reach, use and removal trigger
------------------------------

`ShowcaseVideo.kt` pairs each film cut with its own final poster and one shared
theme start poster. The module's resources reach the Chromium APK resource
graph as well as the Gradle build, so these exact WebP files ship with the
matching MP4s.

A final poster is regenerated whenever its film's visual frame changes;
audio-only changes do not alter it. Because the source project that rendered
them is no longer on any host, in practice a poster changes only by leaving.
This record leaves if the poster directory leaves the product.
